title: Agentic software engineering: the engine behind application transformation
summary: Many conversations about AI in software development centers on AI-generated code, developer copilots, and productivity gains.
body_markdown:
#### Short on time? Read the key takeaways:


- Agentic software engineering uses goal-directed AI agents to plan, act, use engineering tools, evaluate results, and iterate across the full software life cycle.
- Portfolio-scale autonomy requires five capabilities working together: autonomous agent workflows; platform-engineered delivery pipelines; embedded security, compliance, and quality controls; governed agentic AI with policy-based guardrails; and human oversight.
- Applied across the estate, agentic software engineering becomes agentic application transformation: a modernized, optimized, and continuously improved portfolio, with people signing off on what reaches production.
- With a portfolio assessment, you can determine which applications carry the most risk and cost to see where agentic software engineering pays off first.


#### Many conversations about AI in software development centers on AI-generated code, developer copilots, and productivity gains. Coding assistants help people complete individual tasks. Agentic software engineering goes further.


With agentic practices, engineers delegate objectives to agents that can plan work, use tools, execute across multiple steps, test results and adapt within defined controls and with human accountability. The result is goal-directed, multi-step execution across the software development life cycle, at a scale that can reach the entire application portfolio.


AI workloads need modern applications underneath them. Many enterprise portfolios predate that requirement, which puts the modernization sequence on the critical path for AI initiatives you have planned. That's why agentic software engineering creates the most value when it becomes the engine for application transformation.


### Why coding assistants solve only a narrow slice


A coding assistant's view ends where the file ends. It sees the code in front of it and generates what comes next. Modern coding agents can inspect repositories, change multiple files, run commands and tests, resolve defects, and prepare code changes for review and approval. Even so, their view usually stops at the repository.


Inside that boundary, the gains are also thinner than they look. In[Stack Overflow's 2025 Developer Survey](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/) , the top frustration is AI output that is almost right but not quite, cited by 66%, and 45% say debugging AI-generated code is more time-consuming. Faster generation moves effort into review.


Coding assistants do improve developer productivity. They solve only a narrow slice of the problem, though, leaving portfolio complexity, modernization sequencing, governance, testing, security, deployment, and continuous optimization unaddressed.


Enterprises have a bigger problem. Most aren't trying to write a few functions faster. Your application team is accountable for far more than code review, and the roadmap they answer to looks nothing like a coding backlog:


- Modernize legacy applications so they're ready to support AI
- Reduce the technical debt slowing every other initiative
- Migrate to hybrid cloud architectures
- Strengthen resilience and security across the portfolio
- Evolve customer-facing experiences with AI and autonomous agent workflows


Each of these is an application transformation challenge, and writing code faster addresses only a small part of it. Those goals span hundreds or thousands of applications. Portfolio decisions determine where to invest. Agentic software engineering determines how approved work is planned, executed, validated and operated at scale.


### What is agentic software engineering?


Agentic software engineering is the practice of using engineering expertise to direct, orchestrate, and oversee AI agents through software delivery. Given the objective, relevant context, and acceptance criteria, an agent can decompose the work, choose and use approved tools, create or change artifacts, validate the result and iterate or escalate. Engineers remain responsible for intent, architecture, risk, quality and outcomes.


The model covers work that runs across 10 areas: portfolio assessment, requirements, architecture and design, implementation and modernization, testing and quality engineering, documentation, security and compliance, release and deployment, operations and maintenance, and continuous improvement. Agents may operate sequentially or in parallel, share state and evaluate each other’s outputs. Because context carries from one stage to the next, work moves through the life cycle without being re-explained at every handoff.


Leaders see where this is heading. In the[Unisys AI & Cloud Insights Report 2026](https://www.unisys.com/report/unisys-ai-cloud-insights-report-2026/) , 75% said agentic AI is essential to managing their growing cloud applications. Only 23% have begun scaling it.


### What agents don't decide


Knowing where autonomy stops helps you scale the rest responsibly. Three decisions stay with people.


**Whether an application should exist.** Agents can tell you what an application does. Whether the business still needs it is a commercial call, and it's often the one teams defer longest, which is one way a modernization program stalls.


**Acceptance and fitness for purpose.** An agent can check a modernized application against the original, but only where test coverage and documentation already exist. Product owners, architects, and business users define what evidence is sufficient when requirements or baselines are incomplete.


**High-risk and regulated release decisions.** Agents can compress the preparation, the evidence, the documentation, and the test artifacts. Authorized people remain in the loop and retain approval where regulation, material risk or irreversible change requires it.


Each of these is a decision someone signs their name to. Agents handle the work around them, which is what makes the volume manageable.


### What is agentic application transformation?


Agentic application transformation applies agentic software engineering across an entire application portfolio. It helps organizations modernize, optimize, and continuously improve their applications through coordinated autonomous workflows, AI-driven accelerators, and human oversight.


This is where agentic software engineering creates the most value. It becomes the engine behind the roadmap your application team answers to: modernizing for AI, reducing technical debt, migrating to hybrid cloud, strengthening resilience and security, and evolving customer experiences.


### What portfolio-scale autonomy requires


Agentic application transformation takes a managed system that connects intent, context, tools and controls across build, run, and optimize. Reaching that scale depends on five capabilities:


- Autonomous agent workflows operating across all stages of the application life cycle
- Platform-engineered delivery pipelines designed for portfolio modernization at scale
- Embedded security, compliance, and quality controls
- Governed agentic AI with policy-based guardrails, so autonomy operates inside boundaries you define
- Human oversight for exception handling, approval, and accountability


Remove one, and the others weaken. Agents without guardrails create risk faster than value, and guardrails without platform pipelines create a bottleneck. Neither one matters without human accountability. The operating model must make every action observable, attributable, and recoverable.


NI, a leader in automated test and measurement systems, took this portfolio-first path. Unisys assessed more than 90 of its application projects in a single month, then modernized them within a year. We then developed an AI automation framework, in nine weeks, that handles complexity assessment, code conversion, test generation, and documentation across NI's wider estate. Those same modernization principles are embodied in the[Unisys Intelligence Accelerator](https://www.unisys.com/UIA) platform, which helps scale AI and agentic AI through automation, orchestration and governance across Unisys Cloud, Applications and Infrastructure solutions.


[Unisys Application Development and Transformation](https://www.unisys.com/solutions/cai/applications/) brings those five things together, starting at the decision layer with a portfolio assessment and the[6R framework](https://www.unisys.com/siteassets/collateral/info-sheets/info-5941-11120-rva-adt-app-rationalization.pdf) for deciding whether to repurchase, rehost, replatform, rebuild or replace, refactor or rearchitect, and retire or retain each application. Governed agentic workflows then help execute, validate and continuously improve the application against the selected modernization strategy.


### Where your modernization starts


Start where the decisions are. Two questions tell you how ready you are: do you know which applications carry the most risk and cost, and who approves an agent-made change to production? If either answer is unclear, agents will accelerate the uncertainty along with the work. A portfolio assessment answers the first question and shapes the governance that answers the second, showing where agentic workflows can create the greatest business value first. As agents take on more delivery work, decision-making becomes the constraint. Organizations that settle decision rights early will be best positioned to scale agentic application transformation with confidence.

## FAQs


A coding assistant primarily supports a person in a synchronous task. A software engineering agent can use an objective to plan and execute multiple steps, use tools, validate results and iterate with less intervention. Agentic software engineering coordinates these capabilities across teams and the life cycle with shared context, governance and human accountability.


The limits depend on context quality, tool access, evaluation, permissions and risk. Agents can drift from intent or produce plausible but incorrect work. They should not receive more autonomy than the organization can observe and validate. People need to remain accountable for architecture, material risk and production outcomes.


At the decision layer, with a portfolio assessment. If the objective is portfolio-wide modernization, pair that with application rationalization so that business priorities, dependencies and transformation waves guide where agentic execution scales next.
